stack: Linux, BlueZ, universal_ble 3.3.0 Linux backend, run through flutter test
sanitization: The real device ID is replaced with A1:B2:C3:D4:E5:F6 everywhere.

Every 14-byte manufacturer-data entry was decrypted, plaintext bytes 0..5 (the MAC) were replaced with A1 B2 C3 D4 E5 F6, and the block was re-encrypted with libre_bm6 encryptBlock. companyId is the first two ciphertext bytes, low byte first; payload is the other 14. Voltage and the other fields are unchanged.
Every other entry (the 23-byte iBeacon under company ID 0x004C) has its payload replaced with zero bytes of the same length.
Live-data notifications carry no address and are recorded verbatim.
GATT values (Device Information) were not read.
timestamps: Field t is milliseconds since the start of its phase. Phase 2 starts when liveData() was listened to.

notes.scanList: rawScanResults[].manufacturerData is the full list BlueZ reported, in the order reported. addedIndexes are entries not in the previous result for the device; droppedCount counts previous entries now missing.
notes.writeTiming: The FFF3 write happens inside liveData() and is not observable from outside, so only connect-to-ack is available: ackAtMs - connectedAtMs.
notes.advertsWhileConnected: scan() ran during phase 2. advertsWhileConnectedMs are its yields for the monitor; all came from the cached burst at scan start, so they do not show whether the device advertises while connected.

checkA.question: Does scan() miss readings whose voltage recurs because BlueZ already holds that fake company ID?
observed: BlueZ keeps every block seen under its own fake company ID. The list only grows (12 entries at start, 13 at +60863 ms in phase 1, 15 by the end of phase 3). No entry was ever dropped.
New entries are appended at the end; existing entries keep their order. No other signal marks which entry is current.
Raw scan results keep arriving every ~1.5 to 7 s with an unchanged list (driven by RSSI changes).
Live data read 14.08 V for the entire session, which is already a cached key, so a recurring reading is invisible to scan() by construction.
scan() yielded the whole cached list (11 readings, 13.97..14.14 V) within ~10 ms of start, then only entries that appeared new (one in phase 1).
checkA.interpretation: Confirmed in effect: recurring readings are invisible to scan() on BlueZ, and the first result replays stale cached readings as if current.

checkB.question: Does liveData() work in a fresh process without a prior scan?
checkB.observed: No frames. liveData emitted UniversalBleException deviceNotFound "Unknown deviceId:A1:B2:C3:D4:E5:F6" 116 ms after listen, then closed. bluetoothctl showed Connected: no before and after; BlueZ never connected. Not a 60 s timeout.
checkB.cause: The universal_ble Linux backend only resolves device IDs it has added to its own device map, which is filled during startScan.
